title: Hybrid deployments amortization & decision worksheet (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working worksheet and narrative to help the product + finance + solutions teams choose between on‑prem, VPC, or hybrid private deployment offers. Focus is on amortization assumptions, license/support bundling, and operational levers that materially change 3–5 year ROI. This doc is explicitly a draft: goal is to converge on a small set of spreadsheet tabs and a clean recommendation to use in quoting kits and sales playbooks.

Quick summary (working):
- Short answer: for pilots and <20 racks equivalent, VPC-focused private offering (managed control plane + dedicated single-tenant pools) + modular support add-on is typically lower TCO over 3 years.
- For large steady-state (>=50–100 racks equivalent) with strict data locality, on‑prem can beat VPC only if hardware refresh cycle, utilization and financing terms are tightly negotiated and support SLAs are limited.
- Biggest sensitivities: effective utilization (batching/caching), hardware discount & refresh timing, support uplift cost, and model retraining frequency.

Assumptions to capture in the spreadsheet (each should be a top-level input cell):
- Start date, analysis horizon (months/years), discount rate.
- Workload profile: avg tokens/day, request latency SLO, percent real-time vs batch.
- Model mix: % small (embed/rerank), % medium (7–13B), % large (70B+).
- Hardware options: GPU SKU list (A10G, A100, H100, other), per-unit list price, expected procurement discount, rack density (GPUs per rack), power & cooling per rack.
- Financing: CapEx loan rate, loan term, residual/resale value, lease vs buy multipliers.
- Operational labor: FTEs for infra ops, SRE, security, monthly headcount burden and on‑call multipliers.
- Support packages: basic (business hours), premium (24/7), platinum (SLA + onsite). Capture % uplift vs base license.
- Network and egress costs for VPC model (per TB), cross‑region replication multiplier.
- Software license (per GPU vs per-token) and per‑model optional add-ons (quantization toolchain, advanced tracing).

Scenario matrix (spreadsheet should auto-generate):
- Pilot: 6–12 months, 1–5 racks equivalent, low utilization (10–30%), short term financing assumptions.
- Scale: 12–36 months, 10–50 racks equivalent, medium utilization (30–60%).
- Enterprise steady-state: 36+ months, 50+ racks equivalent, high utilization (>60%).
- Hybrid runway: split of on‑prem for sensitive regional workloads + VPC for burst/ML training.
Each scenario calculates: NPV of total cost (CapEx + OpEx + license + support + network + opportunity cost), per-inference cost, and break-even months.

Amortization / hardware refresh logic (unique angle):
- Use a dual-curve amortization: primary (straight-line over expected useful life) and replacement probability curve. The replacement probability is a simple logistic curve parameterized by expected useful life (years) and an obsolescence sensitivity (models/weights causing refresh earlier). The model outputs an "expected replacement month" distribution and expected additional CapEx.
- Allow modeling of partial refresh: e.g., replace 30% GPUs at year 2, remaining at year 4. This captures heterogeneous cluster lifecycle.

License + support bundles (recommendation drafts):
- Core License (per GPU / per-hour license): base access to runtime, basic telemetry, minor model imports.
- Ops Pack (optional, per-FTE or per-cluster): includes managed autoscaler recipes, KV cache persistence, and prioritized console support. Priced as % of Core License or flat monthly.
- Security & Compliance Bundle: includes private control plane, audit log retention (90/365 days), KMS integration, SOC2/ISO artifacts. Price: upfront integration fee + monthly.
- SLA Uplifts: Bronze (8x5), Silver (24x7 non-critical), Gold (24x7 critical with 2 hr response), Platinum (onsite within X hours). Each is a multiplier on base license (e.g., 1.0, 1.2, 1.5, 2.2).
- Hybrid Discounting: when customers commit to both VPC + on‑prem (e.g., minimum 12 months and certain GPU commit), offer blended pricing with capped effective per-token rates and a capex credit for reserved VPC pool capacity.

Cost levers to call out (what the spreadsheet should let us tune fast):
- Effective utilization uplift from Redwood Optimize features (batching/caching): +10/20/30% scenarios.
- Quantization/FP16 vs int8 tradeoffs: token cost delta per model class.
- Support SLAs: convert to FTE and incident cost avoidance assumptions.
- Procurement discounts (0/10/25/40%) and broker/lease options.
- Data egress: multi-region replication vs single region.

Decision heuristics (automated flags the spreadsheet should show):
- "VPC advantage" when 3-year NPV(VPC) < NPV(on-prem) by >= 10% and pilot cost to switch < X.
- "On‑prem recommended" when utilization > 60% AND procurement discount >= 25% AND financing effective rate < Y.
- "Hybrid" when >20% of workload is regulated/sensitive AND traffic burstiness > 3x baseline.

Spreadsheet layout (tabs we should build now):
- Inputs (single-pane, named ranges for all assumptions).
- Hardware catalog (SKU rows, cost, power, density, vendor lead time).
- License & Support pricing (table of bundles, multipliers, and one-time fees).
- Scenario builder (copy of inputs per scenario + toggles for replace/refresh).
- Cashflow & NPV engine (per-month cashflows, discount, charts).
- Sensitivity engine (tornado charts, top 6 sensitives).
- Quote generator (summary page that outputs bullet text + recommended bundle and per-month pricing).

Unique sensitivity to capture (not in other docs we've seen):
- Model churn tax: incremental engineering cost to validate/update models and inference pipelines after a major model swap. Represent as a % of infra ops or a fixed headcount uplift each time model family changes. This can be a decisive factor when customers expect frequent model upgrades.

Examples / quick worked numbers (toy example in spreadsheet):
- Pilot: 3 racks equivalent, H100-equivalent price w/25% discount, utilization 25%, 3‑year NPV delta between VPC and on-prem approx $120k favoring VPC (dominated by lower upfront and no refresh risk).
- Enterprise: 80 racks equivalent, utilization 68%, procurement discount 35%, on‑prem NPV lower by ~$1.2M over 3 years if support kept at Silver.
(These are illustrative and should be recomputed once inputs are firm.)

Open questions / things to validate with finance and sales:
- Preferred discounting/financing terms to model for enterprise (effective interest rates and residual value).
- Acceptable bucketization of GPU SKUs for quoting (do sales want fine-grained SKUs or 3 canonical buckets?).
- Typical lead times and default procurement assumptions for enterprise customers.
- What haircuts do sales apply to utilization assumptions in the field (i.e., do they assume < actual utilization)?

Next actions (owners & timeline):
- Build spreadsheet skeleton with tabs listed above — owner: Marco (ETA: 1 week).
- Add hardware catalog and vendor list — owner: Priya (ETA: 2 weeks).
- Validate amortization & replacement curve with finance (sample interest/lease inputs) — owner: Ethan (ETA: 1 week).
- Run 3 customer anonymized case studies (pilot, scale, enterprise) to sanity-check results — owner: Solutions Eng (Sofia) (ETA: 3 weeks).

Notes to self / rough todo list (scratch):
- Add toggle for per-token license vs per-GPU license; some customers prefer one or the other.
- Consider adding churn scenarios for training cost vs inference serving cost.
- Make the quote generator output both a CSV for CPQ and a short PDF one-pager.

If you're reading this and have a template or prior spreadsheets that capture amortization probabilities or partial-refresh models, drop a version link here and I'll fold it in.

End of doc (working draft)
